technique_why: A sunset landscape of big, simple bands (sky, mountains, golden hills, lavender rows) is exactly what a back-to-front paint-along teaches, and every texture is one repeated mark a beginner can make.
subject: A striped hot-air balloon floating over a sunset valley, with violet mountains, a small lake, golden hills, a lone tree, and rows of lavender running toward the horizon.
focal_point: The striped balloon high on the left, with the low sun and the lavender rows leading the eye back to the middle.
light: A low setting sun just above the mountains, a little left of center, lights everything from behind: lit edges face the sun (the lower edges of the clouds, the right side of the balloon, the left side of the tree).
why: We go back to front: the sunset sky and clouds first, then the far mountains and lake, the golden hills, the tree and bushes, and the lavender field, each painted straight over the dry layer behind it. The balloon, the focal point, comes last over the dry sky so the painter can give it full attention, with its stripes, shading and light as separate steps.

things.name: The sunset sky
things.why: A smooth gradient from blue at the top to orange and gold at the horizon, blended wet in one go.

things.name: The sunset clouds
things.why: Soft coral clouds on the dry sky, lit on the edges that face the sun.
things.plain: the plain coral-red cloud shapes with no lit edges
things.left_out: The many small separate cloud puffs are merged into a few big soft masses.

things.name: The setting sun
things.why: A small pale disk that is flat in the picture.
things.left_out: The soft glow ring around the sun is left to the sky blend.

things.name: The far violet mountains
things.why: A far range painted as big soft shapes, with darker lower ridges in front and no texture.
things.plain: the plain violet mountain range, one flat color

things.name: The little lake
things.why: A thin strip of far water catching the sun; only its base is needed at this distance.
things.left_out: Ripples and a separate sun path on the lake are too small to paint; the gold glint goes in with the base.

things.name: The golden rolling hills
things.why: Sunlit fields, gold on the crests and olive in the hollows, with a little texture on the near slope.
things.plain: the plain gold-to-olive hills with no grass strokes

things.name: The tree trunk
things.why: One trunk and a few branches pulled thick to thin before the canopy goes over them.
things.left_out: The light on the bark is left out; the trunk stays one dark brown.

things.name: The tree's canopy
things.why: A big leafy mass tapped dark, then mid, then a few sunlit taps on the side facing the sun.
things.plain: the dark green canopy, all one dark
things.called: the leafy top of the lone tree

things.name: The bushes on the hills
things.why: Small dark clumps along the hill folds, tapped like the canopy but smaller.

things.name: The lavender field
things.why: Rows of lavender stamped dark, mid and light over a dry purple field, aimed at one point.
things.plain: the plain dark purple field with no stamped rows

things.name: The dirt paths between the rows
things.why: The near soil is wide enough to be its own part, warm orange strips running back to one point.
things.left_out: The shading and light down the paths are left out; one warm strip is enough.

things.name: The hot-air balloon
things.why: A round striped shape built from a center oval and curved side pieces, shaded and lit, with its basket as the small detail.
things.plain: the plain golden balloon shape with no stripes
things.left_out: The thin seams between stripes and the band at the balloon's mouth are left out.

steps.name: Blend the sunset sky

lays.what: the whole sky: blue at the top, orange in the middle, warm gold at the horizon, run down past the mountains to below the hill line

steps.after: The top two thirds of the canvas is a smooth sky, blue at the top, orange in the middle and gold low down. There are no clouds, sun or land; the bottom third is bare white canvas.
steps.why: The sky is farthest away, and running it past the horizon keeps the strokes long.

steps.name: Lay in the coral clouds

lays.what: big soft coral-red cloud masses across the upper sky, flat at the bottom with bumpy tops, sky showing between them

steps.after: Soft coral-red cloud masses float across the upper sky with blue and orange sky showing between them. The clouds have no lighter edges yet; there is no sun and no land.

steps.name: Light the cloud edges facing the sun

lays.what: orange and gold dry-brushed on the lower edges of the clouds that face the sun, the coral left in the middle of each

steps.after: The clouds glow orange and gold along the edges facing the sun, with coral red still in their middles. There is no sun disk and no land yet.

steps.name: Paint the sun disk

lays.what: a small pale cream circle just above where the mountains will dip, a little left of center

steps.after: A small pale cream sun sits low in the gold sky, a little left of center. Below the sky the canvas is still bare.

steps.name: Lay in the violet mountains

lays.what: the whole far range as one flat soft violet, two peaks on the left, a dip at the sun, a long ridge on the right, run down below where the hills will go

steps.after: A flat soft violet mountain range runs across the canvas just under the sun, with no darker ridges. Below it the canvas is still bare.
steps.why: The mountains are the next layer forward, painted over the dry sky.

steps.name: Darken the lower ridges

lays.what: deeper violet on the lower, nearer ridges and the slopes turned away from the sun

steps.after: The mountains have darker violet ridges low down in front of the paler peaks. There is no lake and no land in front yet.

steps.name: Streak in the little lake

lays.what: a thin flat strip of water under the sun at the foot of the mountains, violet at the ends and gold in the middle where the sun glints

steps.after: A thin lake lies under the sun at the foot of the mountains, violet at the ends with a gold glint in the middle. The rest of the bottom half is still bare.

steps.name: Blend in the golden hills

lays.what: the rolling hills from the lake down to below where the lavender starts: golden ochre on the crests and the big slope on the right, olive green in the hollows

steps.after: Rolling hills cover the middle of the canvas, gold on the crests and the big right-hand slope, olive in the hollows, smooth with no grass strokes, no tree and no bushes. The bottom of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Dry-brush the sunlit grass

lays.what: light gold dry-brushed in short sloping strokes over the near hill crests and the big right-hand slope, the far hills left smooth

steps.after: The near hill crests and the big right-hand slope show broken light-gold grass strokes; the far hills stay smooth. There is no tree or bushes yet, and the bottom of the canvas is bare.
steps.unit: The sunlit grass on the hills

steps.name: Pull the tree trunk

lays.what: the lone tree's trunk on the right hilltop, wide at the base and splitting into a few branches that taper upward

steps.after: A bare dark brown trunk with a few tapering branches stands on the right hilltop against the sky. There are no leaves or bushes, and the bottom of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Dab the dark greens

lays.what: the whole rounded tree canopy over the branches, tapped in dark green with a few gaps
small dark green clumps along the folds of the hills and the bottom edge of the golden slopes

steps.after: The tree has a full dark green canopy, and dark green bush clumps sit along the hill folds, all one flat dark with no lighter leaves. The bottom of the canvas is bare.
steps.why: One loaded stiff brush and one dark green taps the canopy and every bush the same way.
steps.unit: The tree's canopy and the bushes

steps.name: Dab the middle greens

lays.what: mid green taps over most of the canopy, more on the left, leaving dark on the right and underneath
mid green taps on the tops of the bush clumps, dark left at their bases

steps.after: The canopy and bushes have mid green over their tops and left sides with dark green still under them. There are no sunlit leaves yet, and the bottom of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Tap the sunlit leaves

lays.what: a few light yellow-green taps on the left side and top of the canopy, facing the sun
a few light yellow-green taps on the sun side of the bush tops

steps.after: The tree and bushes catch a few light yellow-green leaves on the side facing the sun, with mid and dark green still showing. The bottom of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Lay in the purple field

lays.what: the whole bottom of the canvas from the foot of the hills down: lavender purple at the back blending into dark shadow purple in front

steps.after: The bottom third of the canvas is a smooth purple field, lighter at the back and darker in front, with no rows, stamps or paths.
steps.why: The field goes on first and dries, so the rows are stamped over it and never painted around.

steps.name: Pull in the dirt paths

lays.what: warm orange-brown strips between the rows, two wide paths in front and thin strips at the sides, all aimed at one dot below the center of the hills

steps.after: Warm orange-brown dirt strips fan out from one point below the hills across the dark purple field, wide in front and thin at the back. There are no lavender stamps yet.
steps.unit: The dirt paths and lavender rows

steps.name: Stamp the dark lavender rows

lays.what: blunt lavender purple stamps along every row between the paths, small and tight at the back, big and wide apart in front

steps.after: Rows of blunt lavender purple stamps run back between the dirt paths, small at the back and big in front, with the dark field showing between them. There is no lighter lavender yet.

steps.name: Stamp the middle lavender

lays.what: mid lavender stamps over most of each row, the dark left at the bottom of every row and between the stamps

steps.after: The rows are mostly mid lavender with dark purple still at the bottom of each row and between the stamps. There are no pale tips yet.

steps.name: Tip the lavender tops with light

lays.what: a few pale lilac stamps on the tops of the middle and front rows only, the back rows left without

steps.after: The middle and front rows have pale lilac tips on top, with mid and dark lavender below them; the far rows have none. The field is finished; the sky above has no balloon yet.

steps.name: Build the balloon shape

lays.what: the whole balloon as one flat warm gold shape: a center oval, curved ( ) pieces on each side, narrowing to a small neck at the bottom

steps.after: A flat warm gold balloon shape floats in the upper left sky, with no stripes, shading or basket.
steps.why: The focal point goes on last, over the dry sky, so it stays crisp.

steps.name: Paint the red stripes

lays.what: red stripes curving from the top of the balloon down to the neck, gold left between them

steps.after: The gold balloon has curved red stripes running from top to neck. There are no blue stripes, shading or basket yet.
steps.unit: The balloon's stripes, shading and basket

steps.name: Paint the blue stripes

lays.what: blue stripes curving from top to neck between some of the red and gold ones

steps.after: The balloon is striped red, gold and blue from top to neck, all flat with no shading or light. There is no basket yet.

steps.name: Shade the left side of the balloon

lays.what: a darker crescent down the left side and across the bottom, deep red on the red stripes and deep blue on the blue ones

steps.after: The balloon's left side and bottom are darker, so it starts to look round. The right side is still flat color and there is no basket.

steps.name: Light the side facing the sun

lays.what: pale yellow and orange dry-brushed in curved strokes on the right side of the balloon toward the sun, the bottom quarter left dark

steps.after: The balloon glows on its right side with pale yellow and orange over the stripes, dark on the left and bottom. It has no ropes or basket yet.

steps.name: Add the ropes and basket

lays.what: a few thin ropes from the balloon's neck down to a small brown basket built of short strokes

steps.after: Thin ropes hang from the balloon's neck to a small brown basket. The painting is finished.
